reasoning.step1:
I will identify invoice vs non-invoice, locate required fields per schema, and avoid inference.

1) Document classification
- Check for invoice indicators: The text contains "Rechnung" and "Rechnungsadresse" and explicit amounts (Endbetrag, MWSt). No exclusion keywords like "Mahnung" or "Zahlungserinnerung" appear. Conclusion: this is an invoice. Proceed to extraction.

2) Target fields to find: GrandTotal.Amount; Invoice.Date; Sender.VatId; Vat.Rate (may be multiple); Net.Amount (per VAT group); Vat.Amount (per VAT group).
- Rule: If any value missing, return empty string for that field. VAT items are treated as one or more entries.

3) Search for GrandTotal.Amount
- Look for final totals. I find "Endbetrag EUR 19.238,12". This appears to be the total payable. Verify formatting: uses comma as decimal separator and period as thousands separator. Value to return must be numeric type per schema — keep decimals as in input. We'll need to convert to a number using dot as decimal separator in JSON (per schema expects number). So 19.238,12 in Austrian format equals 19238.12.

4) Search for Invoice.Date
- Candidates: "vom: 2024-01-23" (appears next to "Ihr Auftrag: 32400854 vom: 2024-01-23") and also header shows "Stans, 2024-01-24". Determine which is invoice issue date: typical label "Rechnung ... Ihr Auftrag ... vom: 2024-01-23" — but also top right shows "Rechnung 2401440" and later "Stans, 2024-01-24" which likely is invoice date (place, date). Which is explicitly labeled as invoice date? No explicit "Rechnungsdatum" label. Two date occurrences: 2024-01-23 (order date) and 2024-01-24 (Stans, 2024-01-24) which is likely invoice issue date. Conservative choice: take "Stans, 2024-01-24" as Invoice.Date. Return as string "2024-01-24".

5) Search for Sender.VatId
- Look for UID or VAT numbers. I see "Darbo-UID-Nr.: ATU31800708" and later "UID-Nr.: ATU31800708". Sender is Adolf Darbo AG, so Sender.VatId = "ATU31800708".

6) Search for VAT groups (Vat.Rate, Net.Amount, Vat.Amount)
- There's a section:
  "MWSt-Basis 1 17.489,20 MWSt 10,00 1.748,92"
  Then "Endbetrag EUR 19.238,12"
- Interpretation: One VAT group: Net (basis) 17.489,20, Vat.Rate 10,00% (note comma decimal), Vat.Amount 1.748,92.
- Per rule, rates should be returned without percentage symbol and as number; keep decimals as in input. So Vat.Rate = 10,00 -> numeric 10,00? Schema expects number; decimal separator must be dot. Keep same decimals: input "10,00" equals 10.00. Net.Amount: 17.489,20 -> 17489.20. Vat.Amount: 1.748,92 -> 1748.92.

7) Verify no other VAT groups present
- No other MWSt lines found. So single VAT item.

8) No inference beyond visible text; all values present.

9) Prepare final JSON with fields:
- GrandTotal.Amount: 19238.12 (number)
- Invoice.Date: "2024-01-24"
- Sender.VatId: "ATU31800708"
- Vat.Rate: 10.00 (number) — but schema earlier said Vat.Item is array; however required fields list these names (Vat.Rate, Net.Amount, Vat.Amount) singular — developer note said Vat.Item is an array, allowed to have multiple entries. The schema provided does not define Vat.Item; still required keys are Vat.Rate, Net.Amount, Vat.Amount. Based on instructions, include them as values — if multiple, they'd be arrays, but since single, return numbers.

End of reasoning.
